chapter: Trumpet technique: breath, lip and effects
title: Breathing and playing inside the lip
summary: Punch breathes every other bar, explains why one trumpet needed no shared breathing, and how he fixed playing inside his lip.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Well let's get down to the actual playing of the trumpet. Well, and what do you mean? Who was what? I mean now, I'm talking about things like breathing and vibrato and the range of different trumpet players, things like that. How do you breathe yourself?
Well, I'd say I breathe about maybe than every other ball.
Really? That often, huh? Yeah. Do you have to? No, you don't have to. I mean, do you have to? No, I don't have to. That's just your style. Yeah.
Yeah. Then I played with a band named Hughie Swift from Chicago, where you played the, if you're playing, you know, brass all together, everybody breathed the same way. Just at the same time.
What about other trumpet players down here? Did any of them feature long phrases, you know, where they would take a breath every four bars, every eight bars, or something like that?

Well, Dick, you got me there. I wouldn't know because we didn't use two trumpets in the same one band here then. Sometime like a tuxedo band, they would use two trumpets sometimes. But the average band we had them days, they said one trumpet, ain't nobody to take breath with you. Just play your own way, you know what I mean? And amateurs for that. I had a bad way of starting off, but I changed. See, I used to play inside of my lip. And then I put the horn on the outside, but then I could catch the notes I wanted, see. But as long as I played in there, I never, I never could make what I wanted. Well, a lot of guys do that, even today. Yeah, they should play just like this. Make a mouthpiece in there. How you do it now? I couldn't do it. How you do it now?
Well, I play it like this now. And that's the standard. Yeah. Now who plays around inside of the lip way today? I see somebody doing that not long ago.

Some of the trumpet players. I forgot who it was though. Seems to me, Kit Howard plays that way now. I believe he does. Maybe Kit Clayton, I can't remember. One of them, yeah, one of them. But you can't get no power like that. You can't put nothing behind it. I wonder why people started that way. I did. I started wrong by not having nobody to share. Of course, when I was in the army, a fellow named Lewis Mathis called him Chiff. He tried to get me away from that, but I, you know, wouldn't listen to him until I got back yet. And I changed, you know. It took me a good while before I could do anything though.
